source_text.ISS-0995: queue Q-976 / GH #2257: one structured attribution log line per authorization denial, INV-4 safe, sampled.

task.description: WF-03 Step 3c: review commit 1d9f1428 against security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-10 (INV-4/5/6/10 focus).
acceptance_criteria: No raw id/email/token/path/key reachable by log line, metadata or failure paths
403 response unchanged; logging never raises or halts

result.scope: IN SCOPE: secret resolution (INV-4: derives a sub-key from :secrets_master_key), identity data in logs (user/tenant ids), authorization plug on a tenant-data path (INV-10 applicability). Reviewed lib/letflow/api/authz_deny_log.ex (new) and the 10-line diff in lib/letflow/plugs/authorize.ex.

invariants.INV-1: NOT-APPLICABLE - no tenant-scoped table, schema, migration or query touched; nothing is read from the database.
invariants.INV-2: NOT-APPLICABLE - no response shaping changed; Response.forbidden call and arguments are byte-for-byte unchanged.
invariants.INV-4: APPLIES - PASS. (a) Key source: subkey = HMAC-SHA256(:secrets_master_key, "letflow/authz-deny-log/v1" <> <<1>>), fixed label, no literal key, no new env var, no boot failure (master is only read via Application.get_env, never fetch_env!). (b) Fallback: non-32-byte master -> per-boot :crypto.strong_rand_bytes(32) in persistent_term; only constant notice 'authz deny log hash key fallback in use' is logged, no key material. Cannot occur after runtime.exs validation (exactly 32 bytes, all-0/all-FF rejected). (c) Failure path: rescue/catch bind e/_reason but only the exception struct module name and the catch class atom reach the constant line; message, reason, stacktrace, conn, ctx and args are never interpolated or inspected. Key/sub-key are local variables never passed to Logger or an exception. (d) Line/metadata content: method (allow-list of 7 or OTHER), compile-time route template (glob stripped, ^[\x21-\x7E]{1,200}$ gated - verified that newline and space are rejected), policy atom name (same gate), 2 booleans, integer suppressed count, two 16-hex HMAC pseudonyms or 'none'. conn.request_path, query_string, params, body, headers, remote_ip are never read. Caller tenant comes from auth_context.tenant_id (DB-resolved), not path/body. Letflow.Obs.Logger redaction runs on the metadata map afterwards (can only remove, not add).
invariants.INV-5: APPLIES (it sits on the 403 path) - PASS. The log call precedes Response.forbidden and does not alter status, body, headers or halt. log_denial rescues and catches everything and always returns :ok, so it cannot change the response by raising. Logging happens only for decisions already Deny403 (determined before the call); no new branch on resource existence, and Authorize runs before any ID lookup, so forbidden/not-found indistinguishability is untouched. Residual timing delta of one HMAC plus a Logger call on emit vs suppress depends only on the caller's own prior denials, not on any other tenant's data.
invariants.INV-6: NOT-APPLICABLE - no new data-access path; this handoff is the scoping proof.
invariants.INV-8: APPLIES - PASS. The call cannot crash the request: do_log_denial is wrapped in rescue plus catch (all kinds); sampler is separately fail-open (emit on error); note_failure itself is wrapped. A missing auth_context would be a KeyError rescued to a constant line (and Authorize already crashed-safe earlier on that case via Context.scoped_repo_opts).
invariants.INV-10: APPLIES - PASS. No authorization decision touched: evaluate_access is called and its decision.kind consumed exactly as before; log_denial receives ctx/policy_key read-only and its return value is ignored. platform_scope?/1 is purely informational and fails closed (true) on error. No route or permission added or changed.

specific_checks.hash_strength: HMAC-SHA256 with a 256-bit derived key, domain-separated (user:/tenant: prefixes), truncated to 64 bits. Without the key, preimage/dictionary attack on UUID-like ids is infeasible; with logs only leaked, hashes are not reversible and the 64-bit space makes accidental collisions negligible for operational attribution. Sub-key is domain-separated from the master (HKDF-Expand shape), so the pseudonym does not expose the master key. Pseudonyms are stable per master key, which allows cross-line correlation by design (the purpose of the feature). If the master key AND logs both leak, ids are confirmable by dictionary - acceptable since the master key compromise is already catastrophic.
specific_checks.sampling: Two fixed 4096-slot signed :atomics in persistent_term (memory bounded, constant). Slot = phash2({policy, caller_hash, tenant_hash}). An attacker can only choose their own caller/tenant (hash is keyed, so slots of others are unpredictable) and policy keys limited to the compile-time set, so targeted suppression of another caller's line is not feasible; random collision shares a budget and is accepted, with the count carried in suppressed=n on the next line (not silently lost). compare_exchange race resolved: loser counts as suppressed. Clock rollback handled (now < last emits). Hostile volume cannot amplify log output beyond 4096 lines per window. Fail-open sampler means a broken sampler cannot silence denials. persistent_term.put for failure flags is bounded by (class x exception module) and fallback keys by one each.
specific_checks.log_injection: No attacker-influenced free text reaches the message: method allow-list, template string regex-gated to printable non-space ASCII, atom names gated, hex only. Cannot forge extra key=value pairs or newlines.
specific_checks.reset_function: reset/0 is @doc false, test-only, not reachable from any request path; it erases persistent_term (global GC) so must not be called in prod - not an exploitable surface.

result.note: Non-blocking observations: (1) the :authz_deny_log_clock app-env hook (test injectable) and :authz_deny_log_window_s are config-only, not request-reachable; consider keeping them out of config/prod.exs. (2) Pseudonym correlation across lines is inherent to the feature. (3) I did not run mix test (RAM constraint); verification was by reading the code, the design, and elixir -e regex checks, so runtime behaviour such as Logger formatter output of the new metadata keys is not empirically confirmed here - TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-RUNNER own that.
